summary: First complete architectural review of the Repository State Kernel after Phase 114E's containment validation. Froze the four kernel primitives (Repository State, Repository Transition, Repository Artifact, Repository Event) as complete -- no additional first-class primitive emerged. Evaluated Repository Decision against the proposed Transition -> Validation -> Decision -> Artifact Promotion chain and concluded it should not become a fifth primitive: it already exists as TransitionResult, the frozen four-verdict output of validate_transition(...); this phase formalizes the vocabulary rather than inventing a new type. Reviewed every invariant across 113X/114A/114B/114C/114D/114E and produced a canonical taxonomy: no missing invariants and no contradictions, but real duplication found -- three overlapping phase-identity-consistency mechanisms (validate_phase_identity 113B.2, the identity_conflict hook 113X.2, and the structural invariants 113T/113U), plus duplicated recommended_next_phase/report-completeness/push-state checks across the older finalization gate and the newer structural invariants. Confirmed containment does not depend on model capability -- zero model_id/agent_id/backend_id/vendor references found across all seven kernel modules by direct grep; containment for Claude, DeepSeek, Codex, GLM, humans, and future models is identical by construction. Reviewed observability (every significant transition outcome is observable; one intentional exception, manual pcae notify commands bypassing automatic certification by design) and authority (exactly one authority per concern, listed explicitly; one honest exception -- RepositoryState has two construction call sites kept consistent by convention, flagged as a follow-up). Traced full lifecycle connectivity with no disconnected paths found. Produced the definitive canonical Mermaid wire diagram. No changes to the Repository Transition Validator, Notification Certification, Canonical Artifact Promotion, Push-State Reconciliation, Post-Push Canonicalization, or verify-handoff. Execution capability remains unavailable.
